description:

Rohan has been nurturing the art of Sitar playing for nearly 30 years and remains a humble student of music.

Felicitated by 𝗬𝗮𝗱𝘂𝗯𝗵𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗮 award, 𝗦𝘂𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗶 title, 𝗣𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁 𝗩𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗻𝘂 𝗗𝗶𝗴𝗮𝗺𝗯𝗮𝗿 award and 𝗚𝗶𝗱𝗻𝗮𝗮𝗿 𝗥𝗮𝘁𝗻𝗮 award, Rohan is a seasoned performer, composer and teacher, performed in over 16 countries across the globe including India, various European countries, Russia and South America, credited for his dynamic classical solo performances around the world and numerous international collaboration with renowned artists of various genres.

Carrying forward the legacy of one of the rarest and intricate style of Sitar ‘𝗝𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗸𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗶 𝗯𝗮𝗮𝗷’, he has presented lecture demonstrations and seminars in Santa Cecilia and Giuseppe Verdi Music conservatories in Rome and Milan respectively. He has performed in the prestigious 𝗦𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗲𝘁 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗸 𝗔𝗰𝗮𝗱𝗲𝗺𝘆 and has composed for Indian classical dance drama, classical and contemporary instrumental ensembles internationally.

description:

Alaap, Jod, Rupak taal , Teentaal.


Rohan :-
A rising star in the colossal realm of the Indian classical music, Rohan has enthralled audiences at home and abroad. A few notable of them are Basel university 550 years celebration in Switzerland,Indo-German music festival in Germany, EZCC music festival & Haridas Sangeet Sammelan in India, ,Parampara music festival in Suriname, South America . 
As an accomplished classical soloist and composer, Rohan has received felicitations from various esteemed organisations - some distinguished ones are the President’s award ,the Surmani title, Ravi Koppikar & Pt.Vishnudigambar award.

In the current album "Sages", Rohan discovers the deep rooted traditional values and wisdom of a sage through the meditative expressions of the morning Ragas - Ahir Bhairav and Bhairavi.This album features a special collaboration with his sister, the singing virtuoso Koyel Dasgupta Naha. The talented siblings present a light classical composition accompanied by  maestros  in traditional Indian rhythm of Tabla by Sandip Ghosh and Mridangam by Shankar Narayanswamy.The album concludes with a spriteful folk composition.


Available from October 2014.

A unique collaboration between Sitar and Lute representing the confluence of oriental and occidental music by Lute and Sitar maestros Emilio Bezzi from Italy and Rohan Dasgupta from India.
A sophisticated sound scape rising from the swirls of Lute and Sitar intertwined by melody and harmony . A project that glorifies the Indo-Italian cultural exchange and friendship between the two great nations.

title: '𝗨𝗣𝗔𝗝' | Rohan Dasgupta & Pt.Sanju Sahai | Raga Jhinjhoti live
description:
𝕽𝖆𝖌𝖆 𝕵𝖍𝖎𝖓𝖏𝖍𝖔𝖙𝖎 𝖎𝖓 𝕵𝖍𝖆𝖕𝖙𝖆𝖆𝖑
Sitar - Rohan Dasgupta
Tabla - Pandit Sanju Sahai

In Indian classical music extemporization of melodic/rhythmic themes based on the moment's inspiration, guided by the discipline of the Raga/Tala is called '𝗨𝗣𝗔𝗝' and such interplay between the Sitar and the Tabla often forms a spiritual trance like state.

'Upaj' is a unique performance by Sitarist Rohan Dasgupta and Tablist Sanju Sahai on 20th May 2022, Raga Jhinjhoti comes alive with a meditative and organic unfolding of the moment at the Cankarjev Dom of Ljubljana. 
The performance captures the meditative and yet joyful moments of a Raga exploration and an incredible interplay between the Sitar and the Tabla in 10 beats rhythm cycle 'Jhaptaal'. The receptive and relatively new audience of Slovenia responded with warmth and appreciation.

title: Excerpt of "Ragas, Sitar & Improvisation Explained" by Rohan Dasgupta
description:
Here is an excerpt of an interactive lecture demonstration session by Rohan Dasgupta, conducted in Slovenia as a step to educate listeners and bring them close to the art form.

Exploring Indian Classical Music: History, Structure, and Improvisation

This educational presentation offers a comprehensive insight into the rich tapestry of Indian classical music. It begins with a historical overview, tracing the evolution of this ancient musical tradition from its Vedic roots to its present-day forms—Hindustani and Carnatic.

The session then takes a pedagogical approach to understanding Raga, the foundational melodic framework in Indian music. Participants will learn how ragas function, their emotional and spiritual dimensions, and their role in shaping compositions and performances.

A special focus will be given to the Sitar, exploring its origins, construction, and the significant role it has played in the development of Indian classical music, especially within the Hindustani tradition.

The presentation also delves into the art of improvisation, demystifying how musicians creatively engage with melody and rhythm in real time. Through analysis and audio examples, learners will gain a deeper appreciation for the spontaneous yet structured nature of improvisation in Indian music.

Finally, the session encourages interactive learning and dialogue, aiming to educate and inspire open-minded listeners—whether new to Indian classical music or looking to deepen their understanding.

Artist - Rohan Dasgupta
Tanpura - Tatjana Tomazin
Venue - Cankarjev Dom, Ljubljana, Slovenia
